answer: An agent economy can demand proof of distributed presence: each identity must answer timing probes from several distant landmarks, like a lantern flashing from its own corner of the map. A forger's plume of clones all sits in one data centre, so their round-trip times cluster and betray them, while honest agents spread out like a beacon network. Faking a faraway location means paying for real servers there, so the cost is distance, not copying.
